text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Air Liberte main shareholder Groupe Rivaud supports tour operator Nouvelles Frontieres's bid for ailing airline, rather than competing bids from British Airways and Virgin Express. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
-- National Assembly opens debate on 1997 budget today.
-- Generale des Eaux to restructure public works activity to fend off effects of real-estate crisis, expects a 1.8 billion franc profit for 1996.
-- Chairman of futures market MATIF SA Gerard Pfauwadel to present board with report on futures markets and single currency today.
-- Civil servants' minister Dominique Perben calls for a reorganisation of civil servants unions in line with the private sector.
-- People withdrew over 74 billion francs from state-backed savings scheme livret A in September, due to consumer needs and competing schemes.

-- State's need for financing to reach 690 billion francs in 1997, Treasury may issue an estimated 300 billion francs of BTAN and 320 billion francs of OATs, according to report by Parliament's finance committee head Philippe Auberger.
-- Five European countries including France reject European Commission plans to inject further funds into trans-european road networks project.
-- Government may announce name of company chosen to take over indebted defence electronics group Thomson this morning.
-- Milk producers worried over possible cuts in European subsidies and low global milk prices.
-- Leader of France's communist party and his predecessor placed under investigation on charges of influence peddling.
